item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 20, 2026
item.description: WTI October settled $99.53 (-2.3%) and Brent November $103.19 (-1.6%) on Friday, while the Canadian diff complex heads into the week with no fresh public prints.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 21, 2026
item.description: Keystone ran at 94% of available capacity, rail's share of exports rose to 7.1% in June, and the WTI October contract expires Tuesday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 22, 2026
item.description: Yanbu exports could resume today, Brent fell $2+ to its lowest since Sep 8, and the WTI October contract expired after a four-session slide of roughly $10.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 23, 2026
item.description: "Reconstructed edition — the morning run failed; rebuilt from the day's wires and the following edition. WTI and Brent closed Tuesday at two-week lows after six straight down days; the Saudi East-West restart was confirmed; EIA weekly due Wednesday morning."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 24, 2026
item.description: "Flat price rallied 3–4% Wednesday on a diesel-export-ban headline the White House then denied, plus fresh Hormuz attacks. The EIA's bearish 3-million-barrel build was shrugged off. Joliet still dark; diesel cracks over $100 keep synthetic crude bid."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 25, 2026
item.description: "Brent and WTI giving back Thursday's Houthi-missile rally on overnight US–Iran truce signals. Several Joliet units returned Wednesday — the front-of-strip WCS catalyst. Diesel cracks re-testing records; October Merey sales stalled on record freight."

item.title: Heavy Reading morning digest — September 26, 2026
item.description: "Trump rejected Iran's 7-day truce offer after the Friday settle — Hormuz re-closed, ships attacked off Oman, Houthis took Perim Island. Friday's crude selloff is at risk of full reversal on Sunday reopen. Joliet only partially restarting; gasoil cracks printed a record."

item.title: Heavy Reading morning digest — September 27, 2026
item.description: "Trump publicly rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz plan Saturday — Friday's crude selloff may not survive the Sunday reopen. But Gulf tanker volumes have doubled in a month, so the premium is doing more work than the flows. Joliet still only partially back; WTI specs sit at the 96th percentile of length."

item.title: Heavy Reading morning digest — September 28, 2026
item.description: "A ~275 kb/d Midwest (PADD 2) heavy-crude buyer is back online. Meanwhile Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap, and Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries hit its biggest weekend of 2026."

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 29, 2026
item.description: Joliet's restart awaits public confirmation, Whiting union talks reconvene today, and crude firms as Hormuz diplomacy stalls.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, September 30, 2026
item.description: First ICE settlements in days show the WCS front widening $1.40 while both PADD 2 demand binaries break bearish; the Moscow refinery is halted overnight and US tanker enforcement goes transoceanic.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 1, 2026
item.description: Gulf crude flows are back near pre-war levels and Brent fell to ~$96 in Asia before recovering; the product market is in full distress with record cracks. TMW Nov26 tightened 50c to -$21.60 while December sits widest at -$22.40, staring at the 40-million-barrel SPR exchange.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 2, 2026
item.description: Brent settled $102.31 after WSJ reported a third carrier strike group and up to 10,000 troops heading to the Gulf; TMW Nov26 settled -$23.75 (ICE, Oct 1) while WTI rallied, the prompt pricing a November-December egress crunch. Diesel crack $101.74, eighteen straight closes above $100. Pacific Link designated Canada's first project of national interest.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 5, 2026
item.description: OPEC+ held November targets steady on Sunday and crude faded on the overnight tape (WTI ~$89.69, Brent ~$101.67) while heating oil rose 1.4%, pushing the diesel crack back above $100 on the session print. ING marked the ICE gasoil crack $85 to $70. TMW Nov26 held -$24.13 (ICE, Oct 2) with December at -$24.65 the widest tenor; Joliet is confirmed back in service; the SPR exchange bids are due Tuesday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 6, 2026
item.description: WTI hovered near $89.33 overnight while Brent held around $100.28; Saudi Aramco cut its Arab Light official price for Asia to a six-year low as Middle East exports beat pre-war levels four days last week. The diesel crack settled back above $100 Monday ($101.47). Today's binary: SPR exchange bids due 11:00 a.m. Central.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest, October 7, 2026
item.description: Brent December traded around $101.6 overnight (+1%) and WTI around $90.2 (+0.9%) after Saudi Arabia confirmed Houthi strikes on Jazan and Najran airports and a Gulf of Mexico storm formed over offshore production. Tuesday's session had Brent trading down to a $97.06 intraday low before recovering to settle $100.58 (+$0.26); WTI settled $89.44 (DTN). The diesel crack settled $102.47 Tuesday; SPR exchange bids went in with no award announced yet.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 8, 2026
item.description: Hurricane Isaias (75 mph, possibly Cat 3) tracks toward a Mobile landfall early Oct 10 with ~511 kb/d of Gulf oil shut in; Houthi strikes killed three at Saudi airports and a tanker took projectiles north of Qatar. Wednesday's session was sold on the IEA agreeing to accelerate the strategic release and prioritize diesel: WTI settled $88.28 (-$1.16), Brent $100.20 (-$0.38); overnight Brent Dec ran back to ~$102.35 (+~2.2%). The diesel crack settled $105.87 Wednesday, its third straight close above $100. ICE (Oct 7): TMW Nov26 -$24.62, Dec26 -$25.15 still the widest tenor; ARV Nov26 -$15.69. EIA: crude drew 3.2 Mbbl vs +1.7 expected; Cushing built a third week.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 9, 2026
item.description: Hurricane Isaias strengthened to 90 kt overnight with a Mobile-area landfall early Oct 10; BSEE shut-ins more than doubled Thursday to 1,282,879 b/d (62.89%) with 121 platforms evacuated. Thursday's session was the storm bid: WTI ~+$3.21, Brent ~+$4.08; overnight the tape gave back ~$1 on track uncertainty. The diesel crack's overnight print runs ~$111.60 (provisional). ICE (Oct 8): TMW Nov26 -$24.69, Dec26 -$25.35 still the widest tenor; ARV Nov26 -$15.93. The SPR exchange award is still pending; CFTC positioning releases today.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 12, 2026
item.description: Trump posted Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" effective immediately — no terms, Russia silent, Zelenskiy awaiting details and offering conditional acceptance. The overnight tape sold about $1.50 on both legs on the announcement. But the Gulf war widened Sunday: US forces struck Iranian military sites near the Strait for the second straight night, and three more tankers were hit, including the MT Petro Dolphin drone strike at Sohar with two crew missing. The Houthi airport campaign is now lethal: 12 dead and 309 injured at Riyadh airport Saturday, a second attack Sunday, and Dammam airport hit. The diesel crack held above $100 at $102.73. ICE (Oct 9): TMW Nov26 -$24.78, Dec26 -$25.60 still the widest tenor. The SPR 40 Mbbl exchange award is still pending.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 13, 2026
item.description: Russia hit at least six Ukrainian energy targets on Monday, and Kyiv said Moscow is unwilling to accept the energy ceasefire announced Sunday. The market faded the announcement: Brent settled at $106.65 on Monday, its highest settle since September 15, before the overnight session gave back $1.69 on WTI and $1.58 on Brent on the prospect of Russian diesel supply. The diesel crack held above $100 for a seventh straight day at $104.46. Riyadh airport stayed closed all Monday with no reopening date, and Saudi Arabia's energy minister said the response must be equally serious. Gulf shut-ins from Hurricane Isaias fell to 29.63% of oil production on Monday. Canadian differentials had no price discovery on Monday: the ICE settles are a holiday carry, unchanged on zero volume.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 14, 2026
item.description: Late Tuesday a ballistic missile struck an administrative tower at Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry confirmed an attack on an Aramco administrative building that caused a limited fire, with no casualties and petroleum production unaffected. Two more vessels, a container ship and a tanker, were struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, and Iranian officials told Reuters Iran changed its tactics about 10 days ago to increase attacks on ships it considers in violation of its restrictions. Russia reported no strikes on Ukrainian energy targets on Tuesday, the first day since Sunday's ceasefire announcement, while strikes on other targets continued and no Russian diesel cargo has loaded. The diesel crack extended to $112.27, an eighth straight day above $100. Tuesday's settles split: WTI rose 0.4 percent and Brent fell 0.9 percent, and overnight both are bid. Canadian differentials traded again Tuesday: WCS December settled at -$25.55 and condensate December fell $1.00 to +$5.00.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 15, 2026
item.description: A Singapore-registered container ship struck on Tuesday has sunk in the Strait of Hormuz, a second Singapore container ship was damaged on Wednesday, and a bulk carrier struck on September 23 has also sunk. Security data show at least 10 vessels attacked since Sunday and 23 attacks since October 1, the highest tempo of the war. Crude fell more than $1 overnight anyway, as the United States considers easing sanctions on shadow-fleet vessels to cut shipping costs and the IEA reported Gulf crude exports recovering to about 75 percent of prewar levels in September. The diesel crack eased about $10 to $102.05, a ninth straight day above $100. The Kremlin said the energy ceasefire terms have not been established, and Ukraine said it will resume strikes on Russian refineries. No Russian diesel cargo has loaded. Canadian December widened: WCS Dec26 settled at -$26.25.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 16, 2026
item.description: The delayed EIA report for the week ending October 9 printed a crude draw of 8.6 million barrels against a near-flat consensus, and WTI settled up 3.03 percent on Thursday while Brent eased. Kpler puts Hormuz clearance at 11.62 million barrels a day over the seven days to October 13, about 68 percent of baseline. The diesel crack printed $97.30 overnight after nine straight days above $100, a day after the IEA board accelerated the remaining emergency releases with more than 20 million barrels of diesel front-loaded. Ukraine has resumed refinery strikes in fact, with a refinery fire in Russia's Ryazan region. Canadian December widened on volume: WCS Dec26 settled at -$26.75 on 805 lots, and C5 Dec26 fell $1.25 to +$4.00.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 19, 2026
item.description: Friday's settles stand as the last completed session, Brent Dec26 at $109.86 and WTI Nov26 at $101.41. Overnight both benchmarks eased, Brent to $107.88 and WTI to $100.25 at about 04:27 GMT (Reuters), after the United States waived the Graham Act sanctions and duties on Russia that were due to take effect on Oct 18. The physical board pointed the other way all weekend: Kpler puts Gulf crude flows at about 8.5 Mb/d last week with at least 10 confirmed vessel incidents, Ukraine set fires at the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchi depot in one of its largest drone waves of the war, and the IRGC claimed a third tanker mine strike in Hormuz late Sunday, a claim with no independent confirmation. Riyadh airport reopened on Sunday, was suspended again for several hours the same day, and was gradually resuming, with trackers disagreeing on its exact status this morning. The diesel crack closed Friday at $99.35 on the validated history, a second data point below the $100 regime question that Monday's close now decides. December WCS settled Friday at -$27.40 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 16) on one lot, and the November Mainline apportionment notice, expected today, had not been published as of this edition.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 20, 2026
item.description: Monday's settles were split by contract. Brent Dec26 settled at $109.55 and WTI Nov26, in thin trade ahead of its Tuesday expiry, settled at $103.66, while the more active WTI Dec26 settled lower at $98.54. Overnight Brent recovered to $110.10 and WTI Nov26 to $103.91 at 0319 GMT (Reuters), after Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy and airport targets including an Aramco site at Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Riyadh airport. Saudi authorities did not confirm the claims and Reuters could not independently verify them. Kpler's Monday print puts confirmed Hormuz flows at a seven-day average of 10.17 Mb/d, 41 percent below the prewar baseline. The diesel crack closed Monday at $102.98 on the validated history, back above $100. December WCS settled Monday at -$27.50 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 19) on zero lots, and the November Mainline apportionment notice, expected Monday, had not been published as of this edition. Saturn Oil & Gas announced a C$302 million acquisition of Corex Resources on Monday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 21, 2026
item.description: The November Mainline apportionment notice landed Tuesday: Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert, up from October's 8 and 4 percent, with further cuts at Cromer, Superior and Clearbrook. December WCS settled at -$27.95 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 20) on 569 lots, its first traded volume of the episode. Brent touched $111.99 intraday Tuesday, its highest in five months, then settled down $0.76 at $108.79 after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief; overnight Brent recovered to $110.38 and WTI December to $99.18 at 0350 GMT (Reuters). The API reported US crude stocks down 4.93 Mbbl and distillates down 2.6 Mbbl for the week ending Oct 16, ahead of today's EIA report, and the diesel crack closed Tuesday at $105.06 on the validated history. The Baltic Week 42 weekly shows tanker freight peaking on every major route, with TD9 (Caribbean to US Gulf Coast) at WS 830, down 198 points.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 22, 2026
item.description: Saudi authorities confirmed two attacks on Wednesday: a drone interception at the Shaybah processing facility whose debris killed two contractor workers outside the perimeter, with operations unaffected, and an attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport that killed one and injured eight. The US ordered non-emergency staff and families out of its Saudi mission. Brent settled flat Wednesday at $108.82, then bid overnight to $111.64 at 0626 GMT (Reuters), close to a five-month high, on the confirmed attacks and an unconfirmed claim by Iran's Revolutionary Guards that seven vessels were hit or mined. The EIA reported crude down 3.06 Mbbl for the week ending Oct 16 but distillates up 1.68 Mbbl against a polled draw, and the diesel crack closed Wednesday at $102.91. WCS Dec26 settled at -$28.35 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 21), a new widest, with the traded winter strip widening on volume. Russia's deputy prime minister said the first Russian diesel tanker for the US, 40 kt, sails Thursday.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 23, 2026
item.description: Brent Dec26 settled Thursday at $113.17 (up $4.35), its highest since May 4, and bid overnight to $114.47 at 0639 GMT (Reuters), with WTI Dec26 at $100.84. Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters on Thursday, the first such order since February, with no disruption to operations reported. The death toll from Wednesday's Dammam airport attack was updated to two killed. The Revolutionary Guards' claim of seven vessels hit or mined remains unconfirmed on its second day, and US Central Command called the mine claims incorrect. The first Russian diesel cargo under the sanctions waiver loaded at Primorsk on Thursday and is heading for New York. The diesel crack closed Thursday at $107.68. WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.85 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 22), tightening on 515 lots. The synthetic crude verdict scheduled for today does not score, because December synthetic settled on zero volume for a third straight day.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 26, 2026
item.description: Sunday's reopen traded Brent near $115.7 and WTI near $102.3 in Monday morning reports, about a dollar under Friday's settles of $116.72 and $103.27, after a weekend whose confirmed Saudi events were interceptions and debris against claims on the Rabigh refinery and the East-West Pipeline. The Baltic Exchange Week 43 weekly is published: TD3C at WS 1208.13, TD9 at WS 666 and TD22 at $58.22 million, a second straight sharp dirty correction that has now reached the Caribbean to Gulf leg. The diesel crack printed at $97.49 on the latest validated history, below $100 for a second print after Friday's $97.78 close ended the sustained run that began Aug 17. A calendar correction: the Lake Charles refiner reports Wednesday Oct 28, not Oct 30.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 27, 2026
item.description: Monday's settles were Brent Dec26 $115.81 (down $0.91) and WTI Dec26 $101.76 (down $1.51), after Brent round tripped through $117 intraday; the deep late prints near $114.20 were intraday, not settles. Asia traded Brent at $114.81 and WTI at $100.88 at 0418 GMT on Tuesday (Reuters), a second down day on diplomacy headlines from Tehran talks that produced an agreement to keep talking and nothing else. UKMTO disclosed Monday that a tanker transiting outbound through Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile on Oct 23 and disabled, crew safe, the first verified disablement of this claim cycle. December WCS widened a second day to -$29.25 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 26) on only 50 lots, while the January export spread narrowed to +$7.80 on traded volume both sides. The diesel crack printed $98.16, below $100 for a third print. A correction to Monday's edition: the Saudi energy minister's venue this week was Singapore, not Bahrain.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 28, 2026
item.description: Tuesday's settles were Brent Dec26 $113.88 (down $1.93) and WTI Dec26 $99.90 (down $1.86), a two day pullback of $2.84 and $3.37 from Friday. Asia reversed most of it overnight, Brent $115.47 and WTI $101.33 at 0435 GMT (Reuters, Oct 28), after the Houthis claimed a missile hit on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery; Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm, and a single unnamed source said Saudi Arabia had contained a fire near the export terminal. The private survey drew 2.031 Mbbl for the week ending Oct 23 against a survey poll at essentially flat, ahead of today's EIA report. December WCS widened a third day to -$31.00 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 27) on only 2 lots, while January widened on traded volume and the traded December export spread narrowed to +$7.57. The diesel crack fell to $92.35. Joliet's reformer has finished restarting.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 29, 2026
item.description: Wednesday's settles were Brent Dec26 $115.32 (up $1.44) and WTI Dec26 $102.78 (up $2.88). Asia faded about one percent overnight, Brent $114.10 and WTI $101.45 at 0351 GMT (Reuters, Oct 29), on peace talk headlines against the escalation calendar. The EIA report for the week ending Oct 23 drew crude by 1.892 Mbbl, built gasoline by 3.870 Mbbl against surveys expecting a draw, and drew distillate by 1.462 Mbbl, with refinery utilization at 92.8 percent and PADD 2 at 88.1 percent. The Ras Tanura refinery claim remains unconfirmed on its second day. December WCS at -$31.00 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 27) on 2 lots. The diesel crack fell to $90.58. The first waiver cargo has dropped its New York destination, and Iran's strait authority threatens action against the largest Hormuz carrier from Nov 1.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — October 30, 2026
item.description: Thursday's settles were Brent Dec26 $114.88 (down $0.44) and WTI Dec26 $102.00 (down $0.78). Asia reversed the decline overnight, Brent $116.08 and WTI $103.37 at 0323 GMT (Reuters, Oct 30), after a small boat attached explosive devices to an outbound tanker's hull in the Strait of Hormuz, a second tanker took a projectile, and the Houthis claimed a six target wave against Saudi Arabia including a second strike claim on Ras Tanura, still unconfirmed on day three. The Energy Department announced awards of more than 40 million barrels of reserve crude on Oct 29, completing its 172 million barrel release commitment. December WCS at -$30.50 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 29) on 1 lot, after Wednesday's -$31.10 traded 200 lots. The diesel crack fell to $90.42. Imperial Oil reports today.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 2, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27, the new front contract, traded down to $109.75 in early Asian trade on Monday (QNA, Nov 2), down $3.68 from Friday's $113.43 settle, and WTI Dec26 traded down to $100.69, down $3.43 from $104.12, as Iranian and Qatari officials held a third day of talks on a two day reopening proposal for the Strait of Hormuz centred on the release of more than $6 billion of frozen Iranian funds. No agreement has been reached and no flow print has moved. OPEC+ formalised its December hold in a statement on Nov 1, maintaining September required production for December at a combined target of about 31.01 million barrels a day for the seven core members, with the next meeting on Nov 29 to set the 2027 framework. December WCS is -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, November Mainline apportionment of Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert is in effect, and the validated diesel crack is $90.90.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 3, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $104.77 on Monday, down $8.66 or 7.63 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $96.46, down $7.66 or 7.36 percent (Reuters), the biggest one-day percentage decline since July, after Iran's president said the Supreme Leader had granted the government authority to pursue peace talks and the US president cast doubt on resuming strikes. Overnight Brent was up 48 cents to $105.25 at 0104 GMT on a reported US strike on Qeshm Island and was flat by 0355 GMT. No agreement exists and no flow print has moved, with loadings west of Hormuz at about 11 million barrels a day on the last gauge. December WCS is -$30.69 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 2) on 475 lots, November Mainline apportionment of Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert is in effect, and the validated diesel crack is $93.10.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 4, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $103.60 on Tuesday, down $1.17 or 1.12 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $96.09, down $0.37 or 0.38 percent (Reuters), after Tehran called the American reply to its seven conditions not convincing and a senior Iranian official said the two sides remain far from a deal. Overnight Brent rose 76 cents to $104.36 and WTI rose 63 cents to $96.72 at 0730 GMT after Democrats captured both chambers of Congress. The API reported a crude draw of 5.267 million barrels for the week ending Oct 30 against surveys centred near flat, and the US inventory report lands today at 10:30 a.m. ET. December WCS is -$31.25 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 3) on 153 lots, December Houston traded at -$23.02 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 3) on 100 lots, and the validated diesel crack is $94.99.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 5, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $94.62 on Wednesday, down $8.98 or 8.7 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3 percent (Reuters), both the lowest closes since Aug 31, in a session where a supportive inventory report was sold through after post-election statements pointed toward ending the war. Overnight Brent was $94.96 and WTI $87.85 at 0825 GMT in choppy trade. The official report for the week ending Oct 30 printed a crude draw of 0.865 million barrels, distillate down 3.565 million to its lowest since May 2003, refinery utilisation up 1.7 points to 94.5 percent and Midwest utilisation up 4.8 points to 92.9 percent. December WCS is -$31.08 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 4) on 120 lots, and December Houston is -$21.23 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 4) on 165 lots, putting the export spread at +$9.86. The validated diesel crack is $88.73.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 6, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $98.29 on Thursday, up $3.67 or 3.9 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $90.52, up $2.40 or 2.7 percent (Bloomberg via Rigzone), recovering part of Wednesday's falls, and overnight Brent briefly traded above $100 before holding at $99.58 at 0504 GMT (Reuters). Both benchmarks remain down about 12 percent on the week. UKMTO counts at least five vessel incidents since Sunday, close to October's record pace, while Iranian mine claims for Thursday remain unconfirmed. December WCS is -$30.15 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 5) on zero lots, a mark rather than a traded settle, while April through June tightened on 835 lots a tenor. December Houston is -$20.27 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 5), putting the export spread at +$9.88. The validated diesel crack is $91.94. Canadian Natural confirmed the Horizon turnaround complete, seven days ahead of schedule.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 9, 2026
item.description: Oil opened the week softer and choppy in Asia, Brent Jan27 at $97.67 and WTI Dec26 at $90.51 on the latest Reuters snapshot (1134 GMT) against Friday settles of $98.32 and $90.83 (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 6). UKMTO confirmed a tanker fire with the crew evacuated northwest of Khasab and a second outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 7; the mechanism behind both is unconfirmed and the IRGC mine claim remains a claim. The Baltic Week 45 weekly (week ending Nov 6) shows TD9 down from WS710 to WS397 and TD25 down from about WS707 to WS399, while the Brent to WTI spread narrowed to $7.49 at Friday's settle. On the current balance build, November supply runs about 192 kb/d above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound and December about 216 kb/d above, with the overflow going to tank. December WCS is -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots. The validated diesel crack is $91.19.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 10, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $92.57 on Monday, down $5.75 or 5.9 percent, its lowest settle since Aug 31, and WTI Dec26 settled at $86.85, down $4.38 percent (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 9), with Tuesday's Asian session lower again at $90.99 and $85.20 on the latest Reuters snapshot (0759 GMT). The presidential meeting with the Qatari prime minister produced no agreement and no lifting of the naval blockade: strikes are on hold, the blockade stays, and the two-day bridge proposal was not accepted. The Brent to WTI spread compressed to $5.72. December WCS is -$28.91 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 9) on zero lots, a third straight zero-lot tightening, while January traded 620 lots at -$23.35. The validated diesel crack is $86.94.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 11, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $91.49 on Tuesday, down $1.08 or 1.2 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $86.04, down $0.81 or 0.9 percent, both the lowest closes since Aug 31 (Reuters, Nov 11; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 10), and Wednesday's Asian session firmed to $92.01 and $86.20 on the latest Reuters snapshot (0730 GMT). Tuesday's intraday low took Brent below $90 before a partial recovery. January WCS is -$24.40 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 10), wider by $1.05 on 895 lots, the first traded widening after four tightening sessions, while December marked tighter to -$28.49 on zero lots. The API bulletin printed a 9.0 million barrel crude build and a 1.5 million barrel distillate build for the week ending Nov 6. The validated diesel crack is $89.08.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 12, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $92.76 on Wednesday, up $1.27 or 1.4 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $86.53, up $0.49 or 0.6 percent (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 11), after intraday highs near $94.26 and $88.31 faded into the close, and by 0426 GMT Thursday Brent was $91.29 and WTI $85.29 (Reuters, Nov 12). January WCS is -$24.85 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 11), wider by $0.45 on 500 lots, a second straight traded widening, and January Houston widened $0.50 on 500 lots in parallel, while December marked unchanged on zero lots for a fifth straight session without a trade. The OPEC monthly report (Nov 11) leaves demand growth unchanged and has OPEC+ production up 2.04 million barrels a day in October. The delayed inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 lands today at 12:00 p.m. ET against an API print of a 9.0 million barrel crude build. The validated diesel crack is $91.43.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 13, 2026
item.description: Brent Jan27 settled at $95.82 on Thursday, up about $3.06 or 3.3 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $88.74, up $2.21 or 2.6 percent (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 12), taking the Brent to WTI spread to $7.08, and by 0741 GMT Friday Brent was $96.04 and WTI $88.59 (Reuters, Nov 13). The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 printed crude up 4.657 million barrels, gasoline up 1.8 million and distillate up 4.1 million, builds on every major line against surveys that expected draws. December WCS is -$28.36 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 12) on zero lots, a sixth straight session without a trade, while the deferred strip widened on 345 to 480 lots a tenor. The validated diesel crack is $92.32.

item.title: Heavy Reading Morning Digest — November 16, 2026
